text: The Marks card is the single most important panel in Tableau Desktop — it controls how every mark in your view actually looks: its color, its size, its level of detail, and its shape.

Drop a field on Color, and Tableau scales every mark automatically. Here, Profit is on Color — the color legend on the left shows the range, from a low of $540 up to $43,901, and every cell in the table shades itself accordingly. Drop a discrete dimension on Color instead, and marks get distinct categorical colors instead of a gradient.

Click Size on the Marks card, and a slider appears — drag it left or right and every mark in the view resizes at once. Drop a measure on Size instead of using the slider manually, and Tableau sizes each mark proportionally to that measure's value — bigger bars, thicker lines, larger circles.

Color encodes a field as hue or shade. Size encodes a field as mark size. Detail adds a field to the view's granularity without adding a color or a shelf — it just breaks marks apart. And Shape swaps the default circle or square for a custom mark shape, driven by a dimension.
Next lesson, you'll add labels and tooltips to your marks, and build your first Viz in Tooltip — a full chart that appears when you hover over a mark.
